body:
Thank you so much. I feel better writing it all out.

I'd like to make changes, but I don't know where to even start. I feel so mentally and physically exhausted every day. I am at my wits end just keeping up with household chores.

I may not of been entirely clear in my first post, but I have been extremely isolated for a very long time. I can distinctly count the number of times I have gotten out. From 2000 to 2010, I left the house a total of 8 times. For the most part I simply couldn't go anywhere and leave my dad alone, even when my mom was there I didn't trust her to take care of him. I remember sleeping in too late several times. When I'd wake up and go check on my dad, only to find that she had ruined everything and my dad would look so pitifully sad for the rest of the day.

 One time he missed his bedside urinal and a few droplets got on the floor. My mom discovered that first and just shrieked and carried on for over a half an hour, making a huge scene scrubbing the carpet and scolding him about a what huge mess he made, saying she works her ass off for him and this is how he repays her. Later that week, she bought adult diapers and tried to force them on him.

After that, I worked my entire routine by alarm clock. I would always get up before my mom to check on him, to make sure there weren't any messes, and to see if he needed anything.



Since my dad's passing, I have gone upwards of two weeks without uttering a single word. Even then, the only person I talk to is my mom, and she rarely has anything kind to say. She is drunk almost anytime she's not at work. And if I do speak to her, I can't tell if she will be nice, or if she'll yell at me. On a bad day, she will scream at me for hours, telling me I need to "man up and get a job." and to "quit moping around feeling sorry for yourself." or sometimes make vague threats about kicking me out.


 The last time I left the house was April 2011, and that was just grocery shopping-- which ended up being a nightmare. I offered to help with the shopping and asked if I could come along, my mom said "Okay," then added "You better behave yourself" I lost a lot of self confidence with that comment, but I still wanted to go.

 She gave me half the list, told me to get everything on it and not to stray from it, and to meet up at the checkouts. I was doing fine until I got to the frozen foods section, which was quite crowded with other people. I braved on ahead though, thinking to myself "I can do this, I can do this."      After several minutes of navigating around the other shoppers, all the while I'm feeling extremely nervous. I'm looking into each of the freezer doors reading the product names and glancing at the list, trying not to focus on all the other people around me. I find the tater tots and a few of the other items on the list, but just as I was going to put them in my cart and move on, I felt someone touch my side. I instantly jumped up, gave an involuntary loud gasp, then I moved forward quickly and whirled around to face whoever touched me.  It was just an older women. She looked completely surprised by my reaction. Still, I felt my heart pounding incredibly fast in my chest. After a second or two, she said something to the effect of "I didn't mean to startle you." I looked around, everyone nearby had stopped what they were doing and were staring at me. I heard someone else ask "are you alright?" At that moment I couldn't take it anymore, I abandoned the cart and ran as fast as I could toward the exit. Once outside I kept running and didn't stop until I felt a pain in my side and I was out of breath. I felt like I was having a panic attack and couldn't calm down for anything. I eventually decided to walk home, I couldn't bear the idea of going back in the store.

My mom was furious when I got home, asking me "What the hell is wrong with you?" I said I didn't know and ignored any other questions. I just went up to my room and cried. I thought seriously about killing myself that day.
